E1.evidence: Issue #644 (Humble/Galactic binaries, FastDDS action client, rmw_microxrcedds action server) documents a crash ("terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'") with four GDB backtraces through rmw_fastrtps_cpp::TypeSupport::deserializeROSmessage and the generated cdr_deserialize for MultiDOFJointTrajectoryPoint::transforms, plus Wireshark hex dumps showing the bogus sizes are XRCE-DDS header bytes; a micro-ROS maintainer identified the cause ("`RMW_UXRCE_STREAM_HISTORY=160` shall be a power of two. ... Probably this is why your XRCE headers are being mixed with the payload.", pablogs9) and the reporter confirmed ("Closing as the problem has not come back after changing `STREAM_HISTORY` to be a power-of-two.").

units_identified: rmw_microxrcedds (micro-ROS FollowJointTrajectory action server, via the micro-ROS agent)
E2.evidence: In the reported composition (micro-ROS action server publishing feedback, rmw_fastrtps action client deserializing it) no attribute of the interface is mismatched: both sides use the same control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory definition and CDR encoding. The micro-ROS side emitted corrupted payloads because its own XRCE-DDS reliable-stream history was misconfigured ("Probably this is why your XRCE headers are being mixed with the payload."), and any correct subscriber would receive the same garbage; the reporter concluded "even if this in the end was not an issue with `rmw_fastrtps_cpp`". The failure therefore lies inside the micro-ROS client stack, not in an assumption between the two units. The resolving change is also build-configuration only: the user set RMW_UXRCE_STREAM_HISTORY to a power of two, and PR #271 adds a CMake configure-time check (`message(FATAL_ERROR "STREAM_HISTORY must be a power-of-two (not: ${RMW_UXRCE_STREAM_HISTORY})")`) plus README/option text "Must be a power-of-two.", so the case would also stop at step 4 (build).

E4.evidence: Observed crash of the client node (issue body, quoted): Client crashes after a "random time", completely shutting down the node containing the action client -- with `std::bad_alloc` thrown from `ros_message.transforms.resize(size);`.

ineligible_reason: internal (reported composition): the rmw_fastrtps action client crashed on corrupted feedback payloads produced by the micro-ROS side, whose Micro XRCE-DDS reliable stream was configured with a non-power-of-two history (RMW_UXRCE_STREAM_HISTORY=160), mixing XRCE headers into the payload; no interface attribute between publisher and subscriber was mismatched and any correct subscriber would fail. The other composition in the source, rmw_microxrcedds passing the configured history to the Micro XRCE-DDS Client API (uxr_create_output_reliable_stream, documented to require a power of two), was resolved by a build-configuration value and a CMake configure-time check (rmw_microxrcedds PR #271, merged into humble 2022-12-12 as fb2dca62c7881b913a47002a6206bd0029d7bfea; documentation-only PR #270 was closed unmerged), i.e. a build change with no interface change. The missing bounds check in rmw_fastrtps/rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps deserialization ("In any case, IMO this behavior of `rmw_fastrtps_cpp` or type support shall be fixed.", pablogs9) is an internal robustness defect of the consumer and was not fixed in the linked sources.
